citations.name: habeas:coverage
citations.commentary:
Indicatif renders through write_str on this unit-test-only adapter.
 TermLike also requires write_line, whose only behavior delegates to
 that covered recording path. No application input can select this
 unused adapter callback; actual terminal output is tested on a PTY.

rationale:
The `habeas:coverage` citation on `src/execution_coverage/progress.rs` `mod[tests]/impl[RecordingTerm/indicatif::TermLike]/fn[write_line]` is a valid coverage-exception proposal.

- **Allowed form:** The built-in allows the citation on an explicitly declared function with a body. The justification is in fenced citation commentary, which counts as tracked prose.
- **Substantive reason:** The commentary explains why the function may go unexecuted. `RecordingTerm` is a unit-test-only adapter, and `write_line` exists only because the `TermLike` trait requires it. Rendering goes through `write_str`, and no application input can select this callback. Real terminal output is exercised separately on a PTY.
- **Agrees with the source:** The function body is `self.write_str(&format!("{text}\n"))`. That delegates to the sibling `write_str`, which pushes to `text` and `frames` and which the tests drive through `Progress::with_target` and `ProgressDrawTarget::term_like`. The struct is inside `mod[tests]`. `tests/execution_coverage.rs` has a PTY test, `coverage_progress_on_a_pty_preserves_reports_and_plain_output_policy`, which matches the claim about real terminal output.
- **Limit of my check:** I could not read the `indicatif` source, so I could not confirm that it never calls `write_line`. The citation does not depend on that. The built-in allows the citation to remain when measured coverage turns out to satisfy the item's obligations.
- **Scope:** The reference is a `{cite}` of the built-in rather than of a project requirement, so the `{impl}`/`{test}` rules and the redundancy rule do not apply.

I found no gap.
